scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports pings to pc2 (200.1.1.2) just time out.
The partner operator reports the reverse direction fails too, but
differently: pings from pc2 toward 195.11.14.x die immediately
with "Destination Net Unreachable" from their own gateway
200.1.1.1. Both sides confirm the eBGP session between router1
and router2 shows Established. Diagnose.

injection.action: remove the network advertisement for pc1's subnet from router1's BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 BGP configuration (network statement)
Mechanism: router1's `router bgp 1` section no longer contains
  `network 195.11.14.0/24`, so router1 sends router2 an UPDATE
  withdrawing that prefix. The eBGP session itself stays
  Established and router1 still learns 200.1.1.0/24, so the
  FORWARD path pc1 -> router1 -> router2 -> pc2 still delivers.
  The RETURN path is dead: router2 has no route to 195.11.14.0/24,
  so pc2's replies (and pc2-originated pings toward pc1) are
  rejected at router2 with ICMP net-unreachable, sourced from
  200.1.1.1, the router2 interface facing pc2. pc1 therefore sees
  pure timeouts while pc2 sees instant net-unreachable errors.
Localization: router1
Root cause: missing `network 195.11.14.0/24` advertisement in
  router1's BGP configuration
Fix: re-add the network statement on router1 (see [FIX])
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the advertisement on router1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 1" -c "network 195.11.14.0/24"`
router2 re-learns 195.11.14.0/24 and two-way reachability returns.
(A `service frr restart` on router1 also restores it, since /etc/frr/frr.conf
on disk was never modified.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: BGP export on router1 (FRR bgpd) is not advertising its LAN 195.11.14.0/24. Router2 therefore has no route back to pc1’s subnet.

Mechanism: Asymmetric reachability. Router1 learns 200.1.1.0/24 via eBGP and forwards pc1→pc2 traffic across the inter-router link, so pc2 receives the echo requests. But router2 lacks any route to 195.11.14.0/24 to return replies, so pc1 sees timeouts. In the opposite direction, pc2’s default gateway (200.1.1.1 = router2) immediately generates “Destination Net Unreachable” because it has no route to 195.11.14.0/24.

Localization and evidence:
- router2’s routing table has no 195.11.14.0/24; only connected 193.10.11.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24 are present. Its BGP table shows only its own network 200.1.1.0/24.
- router1’s routing table includes BGP-learned 200.1.1.0/24, plus connected 195.11.14.0/24 and 193.10.11.0/24.
- router1’s FRR config shows no “network 195.11.14.0/24” (nor redistribute) under BGP, whereas router2 explicitly advertises “network 200.1.1.0/24”.
- pc2→pc1 pings return “From 200.1.1.1 Destination Net Unreachable,” matching router2’s lack of a route.

Root cause: router1 is not advertising 195.11.14.0/24 into BGP, leaving router2 without a path back to pc1’s subnet.

Corrective fix: On router1, configure BGP to announce the LAN, e.g.:
router bgp 1
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 195.11.14.0/24
Or alternatively “redistribute connected” with appropriate policy. Clear the BGP session or wait for update. Router2 should then install 195.11.14.0/24 and both directions will ping successfully.
